प्रकरणम् १।
हिन्दी टीका सहित
(७)

तिथिनक्षत्रसम्बन्धिदोषाः

तथा निन्द्यं शुभे सार्पं द्वादश्यां वैश्वमादिमे ॥ ११ ॥
अनुराधा द्वितीयायां पञ्चम्यां पित्र्यमं तथा ।
ध्रुवोत्तराश्च तृतीयायामेकादश्यां च रोहिणी ॥ १२ ॥
स्वातीचित्रे त्रयोदश्यां सप्तम्यां हस्तराक्षसौ ।
नवम्यां कृत्तिकाष्टम्यां पूर्वभा षष्ठ्यां च रोहिणी[?] ॥ १३ ॥

तिथिनक्षत्रसम्बन्धी दोष कहते हैं—द्वादशीमें आश्लेषा, प्रतिपदामें उत्तराषाढा, द्वितीयामें अनुराधा, तृतीयामें तीनों उत्तरा, एकादशीमें रोहिणी, त्रयोदशीमें स्वाती, चित्रा, सप्तमीमें हस्त, मूल, नवमीमें कृत्तिका, अष्टमीमें पूर्वाभाद्रपदा, पञ्चमीमें मघा शुभकार्योंमें वर्जनीय हैं ॥ ११–१३ ॥

चैत्रादिमासेषु शून्यनक्षत्राणि

कदस्रभे त्वाष्ट्रवायू विश्वेज्यौ भगवासवौ ।
वैश्वश्रुती पाशिपौष्णे अजपादग्निपित्र्यमे ॥ १४ ॥
चित्राद्रीशौ[?] शिवाश्व्यर्काः श्रुतिमूले यमेन्द्रमे ।
चैत्रादिमासे शून्याख्यास्तारा वित्तविनाशदाः ॥ १५ ॥

चैत्रमहीनेमें रोहिणी, अश्विनी; वैशाखमें चित्रा, स्वाती; ज्येष्ठमें उत्तराषाढा, पुष्य; आषाढमें पूर्वाफाल्गुनी, धनिष्ठा; श्रावणमें उत्तराषाढा, श्रवण; भाद्रपदमें शतभिषा, रेवती; आश्विनमें पूर्वाभाद्रपदा; कार्तिकमें कृत्तिका, मघा; मार्गशीर्षमें चित्रा, विशाखा; पौषमें आर्द्रा, अश्विनी, हस्त; माघमें श्रवण, मूल; फाल्गुनमें भरणी, ज्येष्ठा नक्षत्र होते हैं, इनमें शुभकार्य करनेसे वित्त (आदि) नाश होते हैं ॥ १४ ॥ १५ ॥ (अनुष्टुप्)।

चैत्रादिषु शून्यराशयः

घटो झषो गोमिथुनं मेषकन्यालितौलिनः ।
धनुः कर्को मृगः सिंहश्चैत्रादौ शून्यराशयः ॥ १६ ॥

शून्यराशि कहते हैं कि चैत्रमें कुम्भ, वैशाखमें मीन, ज्येष्ठमें वृष, आषाढमें मिथुन, श्रावणमें मेष, भाद्रपदमें कन्या, आश्विनमें वृश्चिक, कार्तिकमें तुला, मार्गशीर्षमें धनु, पौषमें कर्क;

Prakaraṇa 1 — with the Hindī ṭīkā (commentary) · page (7)

DOṢAS ARISING FROM THE TITHI–NAKṢATRA COMBINATION

(11cd) Likewise censured [in auspicious work] are Sārpa (Āśleṣā) on the twelfth tithi (lunar day), and Vaiśva (Uttarāṣāḍhā) on the first.
(12) Anurādhā on the second, and Pitrya (Maghā) on the fifth; the fixed Uttarā nakṣatras (lunar mansions) on the third, and Rohiṇī on the eleventh.
(13) Svātī and Citrā on the thirteenth; Hasta and Rākṣasa (Mūla) on the seventh; Kṛttikā on the ninth, Pūrvabhādrapadā on the eighth, and Rohiṇī[?] on the sixth.

[ṭīkā] The doṣas (afflictions) belonging to the tithi–nakṣatra combination are stated: Āśleṣā on the twelfth, Uttarāṣāḍhā on the first (pratipadā), Anurādhā on the second, the three Uttarās on the third, Rohiṇī on the eleventh, Svātī and Citrā on the thirteenth, Hasta and Mūla on the seventh, Kṛttikā on the ninth, Pūrvabhādrapadā on the eighth, Maghā on the fifth — these are to be shunned in auspicious undertakings. (11–13)

THE ŚŪNYA (VOID) NAKṢATRAS IN THE MONTHS BEGINNING WITH CAITRA

(14) [In Caitra] Ka (Rohiṇī) and Dasra (Aśvinī); [in Vaiśākha] Tvāṣṭra (Citrā) and Vāyu (Svātī); [in Jyeṣṭha] Vaiśva (Uttarāṣāḍhā) and Ijya (Puṣya); [in Āṣāḍha] Bhaga (Pūrvaphālgunī) and Vāsava (Dhaniṣṭhā); [in Śrāvaṇa] Vaiśva (Uttarāṣāḍhā) and Śruti (Śravaṇa); [in Bhādrapada] Pāśin (Śatabhiṣā) and Pauṣṇa (Revatī); [in Āśvina] Ajapād (Pūrvabhādrapadā); [in Kārtika] Agni (Kṛttikā) and Pitrya (Maghā).
(15) [In Mārgaśīrṣa] Citrā and [Viśākhā?]; [in Pauṣa] Śiva (Ārdrā), Aśvi (Aśvinī) and Arka (Hasta); [in Māgha] Śruti (Śravaṇa) and Mūla; [in Phālguna] Yama (Bharaṇī) and Indra (Jyeṣṭhā). In the months beginning with Caitra these are called the śūnya (void) stars, and they bring destruction of wealth.

[ṭīkā] In the month of Caitra, Rohiṇī and Aśvinī; in Vaiśākha, Citrā and Svātī; in Jyeṣṭha, Uttarāṣāḍhā and Puṣya; in Āṣāḍha, Pūrvaphālgunī and Dhaniṣṭhā; in Śrāvaṇa, Uttarāṣāḍhā and Śravaṇa; in Bhādrapada, Śatabhiṣā and Revatī; in Āśvina, Pūrvabhādrapadā; in Kārtika, Kṛttikā and Maghā; in Mārgaśīrṣa, Citrā and Viśākhā; in Pauṣa, Ārdrā, Aśvinī and Hasta; in Māgha, Śravaṇa and Mūla; in Phālguna, Bharaṇī and Jyeṣṭha are the [void] nakṣatras. Performing auspicious acts in them destroys wealth and the like. (14–15) (Anuṣṭubh)

THE ŚŪNYA RĀŚIS IN THE MONTHS BEGINNING WITH CAITRA

(16) Ghaṭa (Kumbha), Jhaṣa (Mīna), Go (Vṛṣa), Mithuna, Meṣa, Kanyā, Ali (Vṛścika), Taulin (Tulā), Dhanus, Karka, Mṛga (Makara), Siṃha — these are the śūnya (void) rāśis (signs) in the months beginning with Caitra.

[ṭīkā] The void signs are stated thus: in Caitra Kumbha, in Vaiśākha Mīna, in Jyeṣṭha Vṛṣa, in Āṣāḍha Mithuna, in Śrāvaṇa Meṣa, in Bhādrapada Kanyā, in Āśvina Vṛścika, in Kārtika Tulā, in Mārgaśīrṣa Dhanus, in Pauṣa Karka; [continues in the next chunk]

(1) Verse 13 pāda 4, 'षष्ठ्यां च रोहिणी' — Rohiṇī has already been assigned to the eleventh in verse 12, and the ṭīkā's own list covers tithis 1,2,3,5,7,8,9,11,12,13 with no ṣaṣṭhī entry, so this pāda is unconfirmed by the commentary. (2) Verse 15 pāda 1, OCR 'चि्ाद्रीशौ' — the Mārgaśīrṣa pair must be Citrā + Viśākhā per the ṭīkā, but the second term's akṣaras ('द्रीशौ') do not map unambiguously to a standard Viśākhā epithet (Indrāgnī); reading flagged rather than guessed.

विषमतिथिषु दग्धलग्नानि

पक्षादितस्त्वोजतिथौ घटैणौ[?] मृगेन्द्रनक्रौ मिथुनाङ्गने च ।
झष[?]कर्कहरी हयान्त्यौ गोऽन्त्यौ च नेष्टे तिथिशून्यलये ॥ १७ ॥

(पक्षादि) प्रतिपदासे लेकर विषम तिथियोंमें ये लग्न शून्य होते हैं। जैसे—प्रतिपदामें मकर[?], तृ० में मकर, सिंह; पं० मिथुन, कन्या; स० धनु, कर्क; न० सिंह, कर्क; ए० धनु, मीन। ये शून्यलग्न शुभकार्योंमें वर्ज्य हैं ॥ १७ ॥ (इन्द्रवज्रा)

दुष्टयोगानां शुभकृत्यावश्यकत्वे परिहारः

नारदः—तिथयो माशून्याश्च शून्यलग्नानि यान्यपि ।
मध्यदेशे विवर्ज्यानि न दुष्यन्तीतरेषु तु ॥ १८ ॥
पङ्ग्वन्धकाणलग्नानि मासशून्याश्च राशयः ।
गौडमाल्वयोस्त्याज्या अन्यदेशे न गर्हिताः ॥ १९ ॥

जो मासशून्य तिथ्यादि कहे हैं इनके निमित्त विशेषता नारद कहते हैं कि, मासशून्य तिथि तथा जो शून्य लग्न कहे हैं वे भी मध्यदेशहीमें वर्ज्य हैं, अन्य देशोंमें इनका दोष नहीं; तथा पंगु, अन्ध, काण लग्न (जो विवाह-प्रकरणमें कहे हैं) और मासशून्य राशि गौडदेश, मालव देशमें वर्जित करने, अन्य देशोंमें निन्द्य नहीं है ॥ १८ ॥ १९ ॥ (अनुष्टुप्)।

शुभकार्येषु सिद्धिदानामपि हस्तार्कादियोगानां निन्द्यत्वम्

वर्जयेत् सर्वकार्येषु हस्तार्कं पञ्चमीतिथौ ।

THE VOID-DESIGNATED [STARS] IN THE MONTHS
[The printed table of month-wise śūnya nakṣatras is broken up and illegible in the scan — not rendered.]

THE BURNT (DAGDHA) LAGNAS ON ODD TITHIS

(17) Counting from the beginning of the fortnight, on the odd tithis (lunar days) these lagnas (ascendants) [are void]: Ghaṭa (Kumbha) and Eṇa[?]; Mṛgendra (Siṃha) and Nakra (Makara); Mithuna and Aṅganā (Kanyā); Jhaṣa[?] (Mīna), Karka and Hari (Siṃha); Haya (Dhanus) and Antya (Mīna); Go (Vṛṣa) and Antya (Mīna). The lagna void for a given tithi is inauspicious.

[ṭīkā] Reckoning from the pratipadā (first day of the fortnight), on the odd tithis these lagnas are void: on the first, Makara[?]; on the third, Makara and Siṃha; on the fifth, Mithuna and Kanyā; on the seventh, Dhanus and Karka; on the ninth, Siṃha and Karka; on the eleventh, Dhanus and Mīna. These void lagnas are to be shunned in auspicious works. (17) (Indravajrā)

PARIHĀRA (CANCELLATION) OF THE MALEFIC YOGAS WHEN AN AUSPICIOUS ACT IS UNAVOIDABLE

(18) Nārada [says]: those tithis that are month-void, and likewise those lagnas that are declared void — they are to be shunned in Madhyadeśa [alone]; among other [peoples/regions] they do not vitiate.
(19) The lame (paṅgu), blind (andha) and one-eyed (kāṇa) lagnas, and the month-void rāśis (signs), are to be avoided in Gauḍa and Mālava; in another country they are not censured.

[ṭīkā] Regarding the month-void tithis and the rest that have been stated, Nārada states a qualification: the month-void tithi and the void lagnas that have been described are to be shunned in Madhyadeśa only — in other countries they carry no doṣa (affliction). Likewise the paṅgu, andha and kāṇa lagnas (which are described in the marriage chapter) and the month-void rāśi are to be rejected in the Gauḍa country and the Mālava country; in other countries they are not blameworthy. (18–19) (Anuṣṭubh)

THE CENSURABILITY OF THE HASTĀRKA AND SIMILAR YOGAS EVEN THOUGH THEY BESTOW SUCCESS IN AUSPICIOUS WORKS

(20ab) In all undertakings one should reject the Hasta–Arka [combination — Hasta nakṣatra on a Sunday] when it falls on the fifth tithi.

वार नक्षत्र योगसे जो अमृतसिद्धियोग होते हैं वे किसी तिथिके योगसे अनिष्ट भी हो जाते हैं। जैसे रविवारका हस्त सिद्धि है परन्तु पञ्चमीके दिन हो तो विरुद्ध है। ऐसेही मंगलवारकी अश्विनी सप्तमीको, सोमवारका मृगशिर षष्ठीको ॥ २० ॥ (अनु०)।

बुधानुराधामष्टम्यां दशम्यां भृगुरेवतीम् ।
नवम्यां गुरुपुष्यं चैकादश्यां शनिरोहिणीम् ॥ २१ ॥

बुधवारकी अनुराधा अष्टमीको, शुक्रवारकी रेवती दशमीको, गुरुवारका पुष्य नवमीको, शनिवारकी रोहिणी एकादशीको विरुद्ध होती है, ऐसे योग हों तो समस्त शुभकृत्यमें वर्जित करने ॥ २१ ॥ (अनुष्टुप्)।

गृहप्रवेशे यात्रायां विवाहे च यथाक्रमम् ।
भौमाश्विनीं शनौ ब्राह्मं गुरौ पुष्यं तु वर्जयेत् ॥ २२ ॥

उक्त भौमाश्विनी आदि अमृतसिद्धि योग सभी कार्योंमें उक्त हैं तो भी गृहप्रवेशमें भौमाश्विनी, यात्रामें शनिरोहिणी, विवाहमें गुरुपुष्य वर्जित ही करना ॥ २२ ॥ (अनु०)।

आनन्दादष्टाविंशतियोगाः

आनन्दाख्यः कालदण्डश्च धूम्रो धाता सौम्यो ध्वाङ्क्षः केतुः क्रमेण ।
श्रीवत्साख्यो वज्रकं मुद्गरं च च्छत्रं मित्रं मानसं पद्मलम्बौ ॥ २३ ॥
उत्पातमृत्यू किल काणसिद्धी शुभोऽमृताख्यो मुसलं गदश्च ।
मातङ्गरक्षश्चरसुस्थिराख्यप्रवर्धमानाः फलदाः स्वनाम्ना ॥ २४ ॥

आनन्दादियोगोंके नाम—आनन्द १, कालदंड २, धूम्र ३, प्रजापति ४, सौम्य ५, ध्वांक्ष ६, ध्वज ७, श्रीवत्स ८, वज्र ९, मुद्गर १०, छत्र ११, मित्र १२, मानस १३, पद्म १४, लम्बक १५, उत्पात १६, मृत्यु १७, काण १८, सिद्धि १९, शुभ २०, अमृत २१, मूसल २२, गद २३, मातंग २४, राक्षस २५, चर २६, स्थिर २७, वर्धमान २८ योग नक्षत्रवारके अनुसार होते हैं। जैसे इनके नाम हैं वैसे फल भी देते हैं ॥ २३ ॥ २४ ॥ (शालिनी २३) (उपजाति २४)।

Prakaraṇa 1 — with the Hindī ṭīkā (commentary) · page (9)

[ṭīkā, on verse 20] The Amṛtasiddhi yogas that arise from the vāra (weekday) and nakṣatra (lunar mansion) combination become inauspicious through their conjunction with certain tithis (lunar days). Thus Hasta on a Sunday is a siddhi (success-yielding) combination, but if it falls on the fifth tithi it is contrary. So likewise Aśvinī on a Tuesday when it falls on the seventh, and Mṛgaśira on a Monday when it falls on the sixth. (20) (Anuṣṭubh)

(21) [One should avoid] the Budha–Anurādhā [combination] on the eighth tithi; the Bhṛgu–Revatī [Friday–Revatī] on the tenth; the Guru–Puṣya [Thursday–Puṣya] on the ninth; and the Śani–Rohiṇī [Saturday–Rohiṇī] on the eleventh.

[ṭīkā] Anurādhā on a Wednesday when it falls on the eighth, Revatī on a Friday on the tenth, Puṣya on a Thursday on the ninth, and Rohiṇī on a Saturday on the eleventh become contrary; should such combinations occur, they are to be rejected in every auspicious undertaking. (21) (Anuṣṭubh)

All these doṣas (afflictions) are to be shunned in the Hūṇa country (Baṅga), in Bengal, and in Uttarakhaṇḍa (Khāndeś); in other countries they are not prohibited. (31) (Anuṣṭubh)

THINGS TO BE REJECTED IN EVERY AUSPICIOUS UNDERTAKING

(32) In every [undertaking] the lagna (ascendant) joined with the Moon and malefics is to be rejected[?], and the bad navāṃśa; [likewise] the middle third [of the abhijit ghaṭī] at midnight and midday…[?]; the three days preceding an eclipse; from an utpāta (portent) [seven] days[?]; a day vitiated by an auspicious-yielding portent[?] — one day; and for six months one should reject a star struck by a planet[?], [a star of a] planetary war[?], and the star of a portent.

[ṭīkā] The things to be rejected in every auspicious undertaking are stated: a lagna, and likewise a navāṃśa, occupied by the Moon together with the malefics (pāpa-grahas) — the Sun, Mars, Saturn, Rāhu and Ketu — are to be avoided in all works. And the one ghaṭī of the abhijit muhūrta at the middle of the day and at midnight is excellent, yet the 20 palas at its exact centre (a third of a ghaṭī — 10 before and 10 after) are also to be avoided. Likewise the three days before a solar or lunar eclipse.
And an utpāta (portent) is what is contrary to nature. It is of three kinds: (1) divine — the sighting of a comet, aberration of planets and stars, meteors, thunderclaps without cloud, haloes and the like; (2) atmospheric — gandharva-cities [mirages], rainbows and the like; (3) terrestrial — earthquakes, abnormalities in trees, in animals, in fire and water, and so on. On the day on which any such portent occurs, and from the day of an eclipse, auspicious acts are not to be performed for seven days; the same is to be understood for the sighting of a comet (a tailed star).
By another opinion the rule for eclipses is: for a total eclipse, 7 days; for a two-thirds eclipse, 6 days; for a half eclipse, 4 days; for a quarter eclipse, 3 days; and for an eclipse of 1, 2 or 3 aṅgulas, one day only is to be shunned. For an auspicious-yielding portent, one day is to be shunned.
Auspicious-yielding portents are: a lightning-strike; an earthquake; [an abnormality at] the twilight hour; a thunderclap; a halo; smoke from fire without dust; the Sun's disc red at rising and setting; [continues in the next chunk]

PROHIBITION OF THE ECLIPSED NAKṢATRA ACCORDING TO THE DEGREE OF OBSCURATION

(33) One should reject the [eclipsed] star[?] for six, three and one month respectively (tarka, guṇa, indu) according as the obscuration is total, half or a quarter. [The three days] before[?] … when [the luminary] sets eclipsed, or rises eclipsed, or is half-obscured…

[ṭīkā] The degree to which the [eclipsed] nakṣatra (lunar mansion) is to be shunned, according to the extent of obscuration, is stated: if the eclipse is total, the eclipse-nakṣatra is to be rejected for six months; for a half obscuration, three months; for a quarter obscuration, one month. And if the luminary sets while eclipsed (grastāsta), the three preceding days are to be shunned and the following days are auspicious; if it rises eclipsed (grastodaya), the three following days are inauspicious and the preceding are auspicious. If the obscuration is half, then three days on each side. In a total eclipse, seven days [on each side]. (33) (Indravajrā)

THE VITIATIONS OF THE PAÑCĀṄGA AND THE REST, WHICH MUST GENERALLY BE SHUNNED

(34) The birth-nakṣatra, birth-month and birth-tithi; Vyatīpāta, Bhadrā, Vaidhṛti, the new-moon (pitṛ-day); the decayed and increased tithi[?]; the deficient and intercalary month; Kulika; the half-prahara; Pāta; and the first three ghaṭikās of the Viṣkambha and Vajra [yogas] — precisely these are to be rejected.

[ṭīkā] In auspicious undertakings the nakṣatra, month, tithi and the rest of one's birth are to be shunned. The measure of the month is stated by the lunar month, up to 30 days from the birth-tithi. Among the yogas beginning with Viṣkambha, Vyatīpāta and Vaidhṛti are shunned in every act; likewise Bhadrā, the new moon (pitṛ-day), and the śrāddha-day of one's mother and father; the kṣaya-tithi (the decayed tithi, in which three tithis are touched within one day); the vṛddhi-tithi (in which one tithi touches three weekdays); the kṣaya-māsa (the month in which two solar ingresses fall between two new moons); the adhika-māsa (in which no solar ingress falls between two [new moons]); and the Kulika yoga and the half-prahara (these will be stated further on); and Mahāpāta and Mahāvaidhṛti (these yogas are known by calculation); and however many ghaṭikās at the beginning of the Viṣkambha and Vajra yogas are to be shunned. Among the said doṣas (afflictions) the tithi stands by implication for the nakṣatras and yogas as well.

(36) On the pakṣa-randhra tithis (lunar days) — 4 (veda), 6 (aṅga), 8 (aṣṭa), 9 (nava), 12 (arka) and 14 (indra) — one should reject [respectively] 8 (vasu), 9 (aṅka), 14 (manu), 25 (tattva), 10 (āśā) and 5 (śara) [ghaṭikās]; the nāḍīs beyond these are auspicious.

When [an act] is unavoidable, the first 8, 9, 14, 25, 10 and 5 ghaṭikās of these are shunned: that is, 8 ghaṭīs of the fourth, 9 of the sixth, 14 of the eighth, 25 of the ninth, 10 of the twelfth and 5 of the fourteenth being rejected, the remainder is acceptable for auspicious undertakings. (36) (Anuṣṭubh)

THE KULIKA AND THE OTHER DOṢAS

(37) Kulika, Kālavelā, Yamaghaṇṭa and Kaṇṭaka: [their] muhūrta [is found] from Saturn, Mercury, Jupiter and Mars respectively, [counted] from the current vāra (weekday).

[ṭīkā] Counting from the current weekday, take the ordinal position of Saturn and double it; the resulting number gives the muhūrta of that day which is Kulika. Likewise, take the ordinal position of Mercury from the current weekday and double it; the muhūrta of that number is Kālavelā. In the same way, double the ordinal position of Jupiter from the current weekday and that muhūrta is Yamaghaṇṭa; and double the ordinal position of Mars from the current weekday and that is the Kaṇṭaka muhūrta.
For example: on a Sunday, Saturn is seventh from the Sun; doubled this gives 14, so on Sunday the fourteenth muhūrta is Kulika. Mercury is fourth from the Sun; doubled, 8 — so on that day the eighth muhūrta is Kālavelā. Jupiter is fifth from it; doubled, 10 — so that day the tenth muhūrta is Yamaghaṇṭa. Likewise Mars is third from the Sun; doubled, 6 — so on Sunday the sixth muhūrta is Kaṇṭaka. In this manner the muhūrtas of all the weekdays are to be known.
These muhūrtas are of four ghaṭīs each[?], and are shunned in auspicious undertakings. But there is also the opinion of some ācāryas that only the latter half of these muhūrtas is prohibited, the former half is not vitiated, and that at night they carry no doṣa (affliction). The half-yāma is always to be rejected; this will be stated further on. (37)

[ṭīkā] For ease in knowing the doṣas (afflictions), the durmuhūrtas and the rest are stated: on Sunday, muhūrtas 6, 7, 8, 10, 14; on Monday, 4, 6, 8, 9, 12, 13, 14; on Tuesday, 2, 4, 3, 6, 10, 10[?]; on Wednesday, 2, 4, 8, 9, 10, 14; on Thursday, 2, 6, 12, 15, 14, 16[?]; on Friday, 4, 5, 6, 9, 10, 12, 14; on Saturday, 1, 2, 8, 10, 11, 12. These muhūrtas are censured — that is, they bear as the case may be the names Duṣṭakṣaṇa, Kulika, Kaṇṭaka, Kālavelā, Ardhayāma and Yamaghaṇṭa.
For example, on Sunday the 10th muhūrta is the durmuhūrta and also the Kulika; the 6th is Kaṇṭaka; the 7th [and] the 8th are Ardhayāma, and the 8th is also Kālavelā; and the 10th bears the name Yamaghaṇṭa. In the same way, for Monday and the rest, the said names are to be known at the said numbers.
A muhūrta is of 2 ghaṭīs; but since the length of the day varies, a sixteenth part of the day has been taken here. Whatever the length of a given day, divide it by 16, and the quotient is to be known as one muhūrta. (38–39)

[ṭīkā, on verse 41] Among the Ānandādi yogas, the Mṛtyu yoga, Krakaca, Vāradagdha (the Dagdha yoga — "Sūrya, Īśa, Pañcāgni," etc.), and the Viṣa yoga, the Hutāśana yoga and the rest of the malefic yogas stated above, become auspicious when [the Moon] is auspicious in the manner set out in the chapter on the Moon's gochara (transit) — that is, they abandon the said evil fruit and yield an auspicious one. There is also the opinion of certain ācāryas that the said malefic yogas carry no doṣa (affliction) after the first prahara. And some hold that the said yogas are shunned in yātrā (a journey) only, and not in [other] undertakings. (41) (Anuṣṭubh)

(42) If a good yoga occurs together with a bad one, it slays the bad yoga then and there and bestows success. Others [say] that by purity of the lagna (ascendant) there is destruction of the evil yogas and the rest; and [that] the Viṣṭi (Bhadrā) and the others are commendable after midday.

Other ācāryas hold that when the lagna is sound and strong (lagna-śuddhi), the Mṛtyu, Krakaca, Dagdha and similar yogas are destroyed; and that the doṣa of Bhadrā, Vyatīpāta and the like lasts only until midday and not after midday. The same holds for Tuesday, the pratyari [star] and the birth-nakṣatra as well. (42) (Bhujaṅgaprayāta)

This Bhadrā is the Viṣṭi karaṇa. By the method of reckoning the karaṇas, this karaṇa falls in the said halves of the said tithis (lunar days). भद्राके अंगविभाग ग्रन्थान्तरोंमें ऐसे हैं—मुखमें ५, ग्रीवामें[?] १, हृदयमें ११, नाभिमें ४, कटिमें ६, पुच्छमें ३ घटी हैं; इनमेंसे पुच्छकी २[?] घटी शुभ हैं।
श्रीपत्याचार्य कहते हैं कि, एक समय दैत्योंने देवताओंको जीत लिया, तब महादेवजीने क्रोधसे भालनेत्र खोला; खोलते ही क्रोधाग्निका एक कण निकला, यह खरमुखी, तीन पैरकी, लांगूल चढ़े, सात हाथवाली, सिंहसमान गला, कृशोदरी, प्रेतवाहिनी मूर्ति उत्पन्न होकर दैत्योंका संहार करती हुई। तब देवताओंने स्तुति करके इसका नाम भद्रा रक्खा और बवादि करणोंमें स्नान एवं भाग दिया।
आवश्यक कृत्यमें भद्राका परिहार कहते हैं कि, तिथि उत्तरार्धकी भद्रा दिनमें तथा तिथि पूर्वार्धकी रात्रिमें शुभ होती है; और आचार्यान्तरमत ऐसा भी है कि भद्रा, मङ्गलवार, व्यतीपात, वैधृति, मृत्युयोग—ये मध्याह्नसे ऊपर दोष नहीं देते ॥ ४४ ॥ (शा० वि०)

This is exceedingly productive of doṣa (affliction).
The last (final) three (3) ghaṭīs of the fourth prahara of the fourth tithi, of the first of the eighth, of the sixth of the eleventh, of the third of the full moon, of the seventh of the third, of the second of the seventh, of the fifth of the tenth, and of the fourth of the fourteenth, are termed the tail (puccha). This puccha-Bhadrā is not malefic — that is, it is acceptable for auspicious work. Here the praharas are counted from the beginning of the tithi (lunar day); the whole span of a tithi is to be taken as eight parts, i.e. 8 praharas.
The division of Bhadrā's limbs, as given in other works, is thus: in the mouth 5, in the neck[?] 1, in the heart 11, in the navel 4, in the waist 6, and in the tail 3 ghaṭīs; of these, 2[?] ghaṭīs of the tail are auspicious.
Ācārya Śrīpati relates that once the daityas conquered the gods, whereupon Mahādeva in wrath opened his brow-eye; the moment he opened it, a single spark of the fire of his wrath came forth, and there arose a form ass-faced, three-footed, with tail erect, seven-armed, lion-throated, lean-bellied, riding a corpse, which went on destroying the daityas. Then the gods propitiated her with praise, named her Bhadrā, and assigned her a bath and a share among the karaṇas beginning with Bava.
The parihāra (cancellation) of Bhadrā when an act is unavoidable is stated: a Bhadrā belonging to the latter half of a tithi is auspicious by day, and one belonging to the former half of a tithi is auspicious by night. And there is also the opinion of other ācāryas that Bhadrā, Tuesday, Vyatīpāta, Vaidhṛti and the Mṛtyu yoga give no doṣa after midday. (44)

"Those [sacraments] from the sīmantonnayana and the jātakarma up to the annaprāśana — for them there is no doṣa of the intercalary month nor of the combustion of Jupiter and Venus. (1)"

सिंहस्थ गुरुके परिहार तीन प्रकारसे कहते हैं। विवाह तथा मतांतरसे व्रतबन्ध मात्रमें सिंह गुरुका दोष है, अन्य कार्योंमें नहीं; वह भी सिंहराशिके सिंहांशक १३।२० अंशसे १६।४० अंशपर्यन्त, समस्त सिंहराशिके गुरुमें नहीं। गोदावरीके उत्तर, भागीरथीके दक्षिण—अर्थात् गंगा-गोदावरी नदियोंके बीच जो देश हैं—उनमें उक्त दोष है, अन्य देशोंमें नहीं। और मेषके सूर्य (सौरमान) के वैशाखमें भी उक्त दोष सर्वत्र नहीं है ॥ ४९ ॥ (इ० व०)।

मघादिपञ्चपादेषु गुरुः स्वर्क्षे[?] निन्दितः ।
गङ्गागोदान्तरं हित्वा शेषाङ्घ्रिषु न दोषकृत् ॥ ५० ॥
[?]...व्रतोद्वाहौ गङ्गागोदान्तरेऽपि च ।
सर्व[?]... कलिङ्गे गौड[?]... ॥ ५१ ॥

पूर्वोक्त मतको पुष्ट करते हैं कि, मघा आदि पांच चरण—मघाके चार (४), पूर्वाफाल्गुनीके (१) प्रथम चरण पर्यन्त—बृहस्पति जबतक रहे तबतक सभी देशोंमें निन्द्य है; अन्य चरणोंमें

And there is also this: that for one from whose [birth-sign] Jupiter stands by transit in the 5th, 9th, 7th, 2nd or 11th rāśi (sign), there is no doṣa (affliction) in the said acts even during retrogression or aticāra — this too is a divergent opinion. THREEFOLD PARIHĀRA (CANCELLATION) FOR JUPITER STANDING IN SIṂHA

(49) When Jupiter is in Siṃha and in the Siṃha [navāṃśa], marriage is inauspicious; and [the doṣa holds] north of the Godāvarī and on the southern bank of the Bhāgīrathī — [it is] a doṣa there alone, not in another country, nor even when the Sun is in Meṣa.

[ṭīkā] The parihāra for Jupiter standing in Siṃha is stated in three ways. The doṣa of Jupiter in Siṃha applies to marriage only — and by another opinion to the investiture with the sacred thread as well — and not to other undertakings. And even then it applies only to the Siṃha navāṃśa of the sign Siṃha, from 13°20′ to 16°40′, and not to Jupiter throughout the whole sign of Siṃha. The said doṣa holds in the countries north of the Godāvarī and south of the Bhāgīrathī — that is, in the lands lying between the Gaṅgā and the Godāvarī — and not in other countries. And in the Vaiśākha of the Sun in Meṣa (by solar reckoning) the said doṣa likewise does not hold anywhere. (49) (Indravajrā)

TWOFOLD PARIHĀRA (CANCELLATION) FOR JUPITER STANDING IN MAKARA

(52) East of the Revā, west of the Gaṇḍakī, and north and south of the Śoṇa, Jupiter in his debilitation is not[?] to be shunned; but in Koṅkaṇa, in Magadha, in Gauḍa and in Sindhu he is to be shunned in auspicious [undertakings].

[ṭīkā] The cancellation of the doṣa (affliction) of Jupiter in Makara (his debilitation) is stated in two ways.
First, the Revā (Narmadā) — which runs from Amarakaṇṭaka in the south by Jabalpur, along the flank of the Vindhya, Hoshangabad[?], Oṃkāranātha, Maṇḍaleśvara, Maheśvara, past Broach, and joins the western sea in the Gulf of Khambhat near Dvārakā — in the countries east of it; and the Gaṇḍakī — which from the western part of the Nepal district, from Muktinātha in the Himālaya, joins the Gaṅgā at the Harihara-kṣetra at Patna, and west of which lie Mount Māna and the Sārasvata country up to the sea north-west of Dvārakā — in those countries; and the Śoṇa river — to its south, Odisha, Sirguja, Lohardaga, Suhta, Sagaḍ, Bihar and the rest, and to its north Bundelkhand, Prayāgarāja (Allahabad), Avadh, Rohilkhand, Delhi (Indraprastha), Agra, Mathurā, Nadīnātha, Jvālāmukhī and so on up to the northern Himālaya — in these countries there is no doṣa of Jupiter in Makara.
But in Koṅkaṇa (the sea-coast 140 miles south of Bombay), in the Gauḍa country (Gauḍa, Bengal, Maldah, Purnia, Jannatabad), in the Magadha country (the districts of Gayā and Patna), and in the Sindhu country (between Attock and Sherm, which is called the Sindhu-sāgara) — in these countries auspicious undertakings are prohibited.
For countries falling outside both these divisions, by the opinion of another work 60 days are to be shunned. And within Makara only the Makara navāṃśa is prohibited, not the whole of Jupiter's transit of Makara, nor for all countries.* (52) (Śālinī)

THE EXCEPTION (APAVĀDA) TO THE DOṢA OF THE LOST YEAR (LUPTA-SAṂVATSARA)

(53) If, having gone by aticāra (accelerated motion) into a sign other than Go (Vṛṣa), Aja (Meṣa), Antya (Mīna) and Kumbha, Jupiter when retrograde does not return to the former sign, then that is [called] the lost year; and it is exceedingly censured here for auspicious [undertakings] in the tract between the Revā and the river of the gods (the Gaṅgā).

[ṭīkā, completing verse 53] …and in the countries of the Bhāgīrathī (Gaṅgā) the doṣa (affliction) of the lost year obtains, and nowhere else. By the opinion of other ācāryas, when Jupiter and Venus stand in mutual seventh signs (from one to the seventh from it) there is, in the said countries, a doṣa equal to that of combustion. (53) (Vaṃśastha)

THE COMMENCEMENT OF THE WEEKDAY

(54) [Take] the yojanas east or west of the meridian, less a quarter[?]; …subtracted or added[?] from half the day; less or more by the difference thence arising[?] — [thus is found] the entry of the day-lord, above or below [sunrise].

[ṭīkā] Stretch a straight line from Laṅkā to Sumeru; whatever places fall beneath it constitute the central meridian. The distance in yojanas (one yojana being four kośa) by which any country lies from that meridian is called the deśāntara-yojanas. Deduct a quarter of those yojanas, and [apply the remainder] to fifteen (15) — adding if the place is east[erly], subtracting if west. On the day for which the weekday-entry is to be found, in the half-day of that day, [take] the deśāntara thus made less or greater than fifteen: if it exceeds 15, subtract 15 from it; if it is less than 15, subtract it from [the half-day] — this gives the commencement of the weekday. Example: the city of Kāśī lies 63 yojanas east of the central meridian at Kurukṣetra; deducting a quarter gives 47;15. Being an eastern longitude, subtracting 47 palas from 15 gives 14;13. Since this is less than the half-day 17;2, subtracting 14;13 leaves a remainder of 2;49. As the computed figure is less than the half-day, the weekday-entry will occur 2;49 after sunrise. (54) (Upajāti)

(55) [The count] from the weekday, in ghaṭikās, doubled[?]; …[?] with the remainder removed; increased by one …[?]; [divided] by seven (naga) — [thus] the lords of the kāla-horās, from the day-lord, in order.

बुधकी होरा हुई। यहां वारप्रवृत्ति केवल कालहोराके निमित्त है, और कार्योंमें वार सूर्योदयसे ही माना जाता है—यह वसिष्ठसिद्धान्तमें लिखा है ॥ ५५ ॥ (अनु०)।

कालहोराप्रयोजनम्

वारे प्रोक्तं कालहोरासु तस्य धिष्ण्ये प्रोक्तं स्वामितिथ्यंशके[?]ऽस्य ।
कुर्याद्दिक्शूलादि[?] चिन्त्यं क्षणेषु नैवोद्धृष्यः[?] परिवेश्चापि[?] दण्डः ॥ ५६ ॥

कालहोराका प्रयोजन है कि, जो कार्य जिस वारमें करना कहा है वह उसकी कालहोरामें हर एक वारमें कर लेना। जैसे रविवारके दिन प्रवेशका निषेध है, परन्तु चन्द्र, बुध, गुरु, शुक्रके होरामें रविवारके दिन भी आवश्यकमें प्रवेश कर लेना। ऐसे ही जिस नक्षत्रमें जो कार्य नहीं करना कहा है, उसमें यदि आवश्यक हो तो उस नक्षत्रमें जिस मुहूर्तमें पूर्वोक्त नक्षत्रके स्वामीकी कालहोरा हो, उसमें वह कृत्य कर लेना। मुहूर्तके स्वामी विवाहप्रकरणमें कहे हैं। उक्त विषयके मुहूर्तमें इतना अवश्य स्मरण चाहिये कि दिक्शूल तथा परिदण्डादि विचार छोड़ें नहीं—इनका विचार यात्राप्रकरणमें है ॥ ५६ ॥ (शालिनी)।

मन्वादियुगादीनां निर्णयस्तन्निषेधश्च

मन्वाद्या[?]क्षितिथी मधौ तिथिरवी[?] ...शुचौ दिक्तिथी-
ज्येष्ठेऽन्त्ये च तिथिस्त्विषे[?] नव तपस्याः सहस्ये शिवाः ।
भाद्रेऽग्निश्च सिते त्वमाष्टनभसः कृष्णे युगाः सिते
गोऽग्नी[?] गाहुलराधयोर्मेदनदशौ[?] भाद्रमाघासिते ॥ ५७ ॥

इति मुहूर्तचिन्तामणौ प्रथमं शुभाशुभप्रकरणम् ॥ १ ॥

चैत्र शुक्लपक्षकी ३।१५; कार्तिक शुक्लकी १५।१२; आषाढ शुक्लकी १०।१५; ज्येष्ठ तथा फाल्गुनकी १५; आश्विन शुक्लकी [?]; माघशुक्लकी ७; पौषशुक्लकी ११; भाद्रशुक्लकी ३; श्रावणकृष्णकी ३० (अमा), ८ (अष्टमी)—ये मन्वादि हैं। और कार्तिकशुक्लकी ९; वैशाखशुक्लकी ३; भाद्रकृष्णकी १३; माघकी ३० (अमा)—ये युगादि हैं। इतनी तिथियां पुण्यपर्व

[ṭīkā, completing verse 55] …so it is Mercury's horā. Here the commencement of the weekday is reckoned only for the sake of the kāla-horā; in [other] undertakings the weekday is counted from sunrise alone — so it is written in the Vasiṣṭha-siddhānta. (55) (Anuṣṭubh)

THE PURPOSE OF THE KĀLA-HORĀ

(56) What is prescribed for a [particular] vāra (weekday) [may be done] in the kāla-horās of that [lord]; what is prescribed for [a particular] nakṣatra (lunar mansion), in the [horā of] its lord[?] … One should [nevertheless] consider the dik-śūla[?] and the like at those moments; and [the] paridaṇḍa[?] is not to be disregarded[?].

[ṭīkā] The purpose of the kāla-horā is this: an act that is prescribed to be done on a particular weekday may be done on any weekday in the kāla-horā of that [weekday's lord]. For example, house-entry is prohibited on a Sunday; yet in the horā of the Moon, Mercury, Jupiter or Venus, entry may in case of necessity be made even on a Sunday. In the same way, where an act is prohibited in a particular nakṣatra, then if it be unavoidable, that act may be performed in that nakṣatra during the muhūrta in which the kāla-horā of the lord of the aforesaid nakṣatra falls. The lords of the muhūrtas are stated in the marriage chapter. In the muhūrta for the said purpose this much must be borne in mind — that the considerations of dik-śūla and paridaṇḍa and the like are not to be dropped; their consideration is given in the chapter on journeys. (56) (Śālinī)

DETERMINATION OF THE MANVĀDI AND YUGĀDI [TITHIS], AND THEIR PROHIBITION

(57) [The verse enumerates the manvādi and yugādi tithis by month and numeral-word; the printed text is substantially corrupt in the scan and is not rendered word-for-word. Its content is given by the ṭīkā below.]

Here ends the first chapter, the Śubhāśubha-prakaraṇa, in the Muhūrta-Cintāmaṇi. (1)

[ṭīkā] The 3rd and 15th of the bright fortnight of Caitra; the 15th and 12th of the bright fortnight of Kārtika; the 10th and 15th of the bright fortnight of Āṣāḍha; the 15th of Jyeṣṭha and of Phālguna; the [?] of the bright fortnight of Āśvina; the 7th of the bright fortnight of Māgha; the 11th of the bright fortnight of Pauṣa; the 3rd of the bright fortnight of Bhādrapada; and the 30th (new moon) and 8th (aṣṭamī) of the dark fortnight of Śrāvaṇa — these are the manvādi [tithis].
